claim: WhatsApp update breaks Baileys authentication, requiring re-pairing.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that after a recent WhatsApp update, their Baileys-based automation stopped working due to authentication failures. They had to regenerate the QR code and re-link the device to restore functionality. Multiple other users confirm the same issue.

claim: Session loss in whatsapp-web.js after WhatsApp update.
paraphrased_evidence: A user describes that their whatsapp-web.js session is lost every few days, requiring them to re-authenticate. They mention that this has been happening more frequently after a recent WhatsApp update. The issue has many comments from users with similar experiences.

claim: Whatsmeow multi-device sync broken after WhatsApp update.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that after a WhatsApp update, their whatsmeow-based bot cannot sync messages across devices. They have to manually restart the bot and re-authenticate to get it working again. The maintainer acknowledges the issue and is working on a fix.

claim: Rate limiting causes temporary ban of WhatsApp number.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that their WhatsApp number was temporarily banned after sending too many messages in a short period using Baileys. They had to wait 24 hours and implement delays to avoid future bans. Other users share their experiences with rate limits and bans.

claim: Number banned after bulk messaging with whatsapp-web.js.
paraphrased_evidence: A user describes that their phone number was permanently banned after sending bulk messages using whatsapp-web.js. They lost access to their WhatsApp account and had to get a new number. The thread discusses strategies to avoid bans, such as using multiple numbers and rotating them.

claim: Whatsmeow user banned after high-frequency messaging.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that their number was banned after sending messages too quickly with whatsmeow. They had to implement a delay of several seconds between messages to avoid future bans. The maintainer suggests using exponential backoff.

claim: No way to retrieve message history with Baileys.
paraphrased_evidence: A user asks how to retrieve old messages using Baileys, as the library does not support history sync. They need historical data for a customer support application. Other users suggest workarounds like scraping from the phone or using third-party tools.

claim: Whatsapp-web.js cannot sync chat history.
paraphrased_evidence: A user requests the ability to sync chat history in whatsapp-web.js for compliance purposes. The maintainer explains that this is not possible due to WhatsApp's protocol limitations. Users discuss manual export workarounds.

claim: Baileys lacks group management features.
paraphrased_evidence: A user requests the ability to add/remove group members and get participant lists using Baileys. The maintainer says these features are not implemented. Users share custom scripts to handle group operations.

claim: Whatsapp-web.js cannot send bulk messages to groups.
paraphrased_evidence: A user wants to send a message to multiple groups using whatsapp-web.js but finds no built-in support. They have to loop through groups and send individually, which is slow and risks rate limiting.

claim: Baileys does not support catalog/product messages.
paraphrased_evidence: A user asks how to send product catalog messages using Baileys for their e-commerce business. The maintainer says this feature is not supported. Users discuss workarounds using raw protocol buffers.

claim: Whatsapp-web.js lacks broadcast list support.
paraphrased_evidence: A user requests broadcast list functionality in whatsapp-web.js for sending marketing messages. The maintainer says it's not implemented. Users suggest using group messages as a workaround.

claim: Baileys maintainer overwhelmed by constant updates.
paraphrased_evidence: The maintainer of Baileys posts an issue asking for help because they cannot keep up with WhatsApp's frequent protocol changes. They mention that each update requires significant reverse-engineering effort. Community members offer to contribute.

claim: Whatsapp-web.js maintainer burnout due to constant fixes.
paraphrased_evidence: A user expresses concern about the slow response to issues in whatsapp-web.js. The maintainer replies that they are dealing with burnout from the constant need to fix breakages caused by WhatsApp updates. They are looking for more maintainers.

claim: Multi-device sync issues in whatsmeow.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that messages sent from one device are not appearing on another device when using whatsmeow. They have to manually sync by restarting the bot. The maintainer suspects a protocol issue.

claim: Baileys multi-device sync unreliable.
paraphrased_evidence: A user describes that their Baileys-based bot sometimes misses messages when running on multiple devices. They have to implement a custom sync mechanism to ensure all messages are captured.

claim: Media sending issues in whatsapp-web.js.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that sending images via whatsapp-web.js often fails with an error. They have to retry multiple times. Other users share similar experiences with video and document uploads.

claim: Baileys media download fails for large files.
paraphrased_evidence: A user cannot download large video files using Baileys. The download times out or fails. They have to implement custom chunked downloading logic.

claim: Whatsmeow lacks built-in message queue.
paraphrased_evidence: A user asks if whatsmeow has a built-in message queue for retries. The maintainer says no, and users share their custom queue implementations using databases.

claim: Baileys message delivery unreliable without custom retry logic.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that messages sent via Baileys are sometimes not delivered without any error. They have to implement a custom delivery confirmation system using message IDs.

claim: Whatsapp-web.js decryption fails after update.
paraphrased_evidence: A user reports that after a WhatsApp update, their whatsapp-web.js bot cannot decrypt incoming messages. They have to wait for a library update to fix the decryption logic.

claim: Baileys encryption changes cause message reading failure.
paraphrased_evidence: A user cannot read incoming messages after WhatsApp changed its encryption protocol. The Baileys library needs an update to handle the new encryption. Users discuss temporary workarounds.
